newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks break record streak on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks break record streak on profit-taking.

text.p: Mexican stocks ended down for the first time in nine sessions on Friday as dealers decided to take profits in a quiet session, traders said.
"The market saw profit-taking today, and sought to consolidate recent gains," said Hector Jimenez, an analyst at the Inverlat brokerage.
"This could be the beginning of the breather we've all been expecting. Today, however, investors were not bailing out, just selling moderately."
The blue chip IPC index closed down 40.77 points, or 0.84 percent, at 4,821.62.
Trading volume was the lightest of the week at 87.7 million shares.

"Nothing much happened, it was just a normal retreat after the market shot through two resistance levels like they weren't there," a desk trader said. "We saw no earth-shaking economic or corporate news today."
Dealers said the most heavily traded sliders read like a roll call of stocks that led the recent rally, and were headed by Telfonos de Mxico (Telmex) and financial group Bancomer.
Bancomer B shares fell 19 centavos to 4.19 pesos.
Telmex shed 25 centavos to 21.00 pesos. The telecom's ADRs ended down 9/16 to 53-5/16 in a parallel move that shunned gains on the Dow Jones, which ended up 35.06 points at 7,921.82.

Vitro was one of the few blue chips that bucked the downward trend and gained 45 centavos to 35.20 pesos on what dealers said was a favorable market reaction to second quarter earnings it posted on Thursday night.
On the broad market, decliners outnumbered gainers by 54 to 50, out of a total 115 stocks that changed hands.
